facts.claim: In November 1880, the Government of India consulted the Bombay Chamber of Commerce regarding the introduction of the telephone.
facts.quote: In November 1880 the Government of India informed the Bombay Chamber of Commerce that they were considering the question of introducing the telephone into India as part of the machinery of the Telegraph Department, and asked for an expression of the views of the Chamber on the subject

facts.claim: The Bombay Chamber of Commerce advised that introducing the telephone should be left to private enterprise.
facts.quote: to which the Chamber of Commerce replied that in their opinion the introduction of this convenience should be left to private enterprise.

facts.claim: The Bombay Telephone Company was formed in 1882 with a nominal capital of 9.6 lakhs.
facts.quote: for in 1882 the Bombay Tele- phone Company, established with limited liability under the Indian Companies* Act, was formed with a nominal capital of 9*6 lakhs to acquire from the Oriental Tele- phone Company all the telephone exchanges and lines in Bombay and Karachi
